raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR adds a unit-test foundation for serving and streaming in dynamic inference. It streams real engine output through the coordinator reply path and the live client APIs, checking each partial reply against the final result and against the same request run without streaming. It changes no production code, and every test passes on unmodified `main`.

The foundation adds:

- streaming variants of the async-scheduling pairwise tests: every single-GPU scenario, the suspend/resume scenarios with a weight refit while suspended, and the distributed scenarios. They run beside the existing non-streaming tests, which are unchanged;
- five new async-pair scenarios: hybrid GDP, hybrid GDN, MXFP8 Transformer Engine, NVFP4 inference-optimized MoE, and MoE with EP2 and expert-TP2;
- real-engine streaming tests:
  - prompt KV handed off between two ranks over NCCL and NIXL;
  - image and video requests on a small LLaVA model;
  - two live clients streaming through a real coordinator, the high-level API facades, and a cancelled request beside a survivor;
  - generation-epoch control messages arriving during streaming;
- endpoint streaming tests: a client disconnect aborts every open stream, and a non-streaming completion ignores a malformed `stream_options` field;
- test infrastructure:
  - a LLaVA model option in the engine test environment, and an engine-class override;
  - configuration fields for expert TP, the MoE expert count, the FP8 recipe, the KV transport backend, the grouped-GEMM backend and the NVFP4 recipe;
  - a shared test tokenizer whose `detokenize` accepts keyword arguments and that resolves an `<image>` token.

## How was the test matrix determined?

An audit of serving coverage found that streaming was tested mainly with simple single-feature requests. Streaming was not crossed with the engine features that change how requests are scheduled, such as prefix caching, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, MTP, hybrid models, MoE, parallel topologies and suspend/resume. The end-to-end paths that only exist with streaming also had no real-engine coverage: disaggregated KV handoff, multimodal media and live coordinator clients.

The matrix has two layers:

1. **Streaming crossed with the async-pair scenarios.** The async-scheduling suite already has one scenario per behavior-affecting feature. The new streaming variant runs each scenario with streaming on and compares the result with the legacy non-streaming run. The five added scenarios extend the suite to model, precision and topology features it did not cover.
2. **Real-engine streaming paths.** These exercise the coordinator, the client, KV handoff and multimodal media with real model steps.
3. **Endpoint streaming.** Two endpoint behaviors that already work on `main` and had no test: a client disconnect during a stream, and a malformed `stream_options` on a non-streaming completion.

This is differential coverage: each streaming run is compared with the non-streaming legacy run of the same scenario. The existing non-streaming async tests still run unchanged, so the async-scheduling coverage on `main` is not replaced.

## What combinations are tested?

### Streaming × single-GPU async scenarios (31 cases)

Each case runs the scenario's requests in the legacy scheduler without streaming, and in the async scheduler with streaming at interval 1. The async engine sends partial replies through a mocked coordinator socket.

| Group | Scenarios |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduling and caching | `dense-eager-events`, `chunked-capacity`, `prefix-ref-zero`, `prefix-lru-chunked` |
| CUDA graphs | `graph-decode-block-exponential`, `graph-bounded-mixed-prefill`, `graph-mixed-layer-linear` |
| Sampling and scores | `sampling-temperature-top-k`, `sampling-top-p`, `sampling-top-k-top-p`, `raw-prompt-top-n-logprobs`, `processed-skip-prompt-logprobs`, `flashinfer-sampling` |
| Lengths and termination | `length-zero-and-total`, `string-prompt-bos`, `termination-values`, `stop-sequence-keep`, `stop-sequence-strip` |
| Speculative decoding | `mtp-depth-one`, `mtp-graph-heterogeneous-logprobs` |
| Models | `hybrid-mamba`, `hybrid-gdp` (new), `hybrid-gdn` (new), `transformer-engine`, `inference-optimized` |
| Precision | `fp8-transformer-engine`, `mxfp8-transformer-engine` (new, Blackwell), `nvfp4-inference-moe` (new, Blackwell) |
| Attention | `flashinfer-fused-rope`, `swa-off-by-one-sink`, `alternating-swa-learnable-sink` |

### Streaming × suspend/resume (2 cases)

While suspended, both the legacy run and the streaming async run load the same perturbed weights from a second model, so their outputs remain comparable after the refit.

| Scenario | Lifecycle while streaming |
| --- | --- |
| `offload-suspend-resume` | Suspend with KV offload, refit the weights from a second model, resume |
| `recompute-suspend-resume` | Suspend with recompute, refit the weights, resume |

### Streaming × distributed topologies (4 cases)

| Scenario | Topology | Ranks |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `tp2-pp2-sp-dp2` | TP2 × PP2 with sequence parallelism, DP2 | 8 |
| `moe-ep2-nccl` | MoE with EP2 and the NCCL token dispatcher | 4 or more |
| `moe-ep2-etp2` (new) | MoE with EP2 and expert TP2, Transformer Engine | 4 or more |
| `optimized-tp2-sp` | Inference-optimized layers with TP2 and sequence parallelism | 4 or more |

### Real-engine streaming paths (6 cases)

| Test | Cases | What it combines |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `test_real_kv_handoff_streams_imported_decode_and_matches_greedy` | 2 (NCCL, NIXL) | One rank prefills, the other imports the KV and streams decode |
| `test_real_vlm_media_stream_matches_nonstreaming` | 2 (image, video) | LLaVA media embeddings with streaming against non-streaming |
| `test_real_coordinator_streams_before_completion_and_matches_greedy` | 1 | Two clients streaming through a real coordinator with chunked prefill and prefix caching; the sync and async high-level facades; cancellation with a surviving request |
| `test_streamed_partials_follow_generation_epoch_messages` | 1 | Generation-epoch control messages while requests stream |

### Endpoint streaming (3 cases)

| Test | Cases | What it checks |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `test_streaming_disconnect_aborts_every_open_stream` | 2 (chat, completions) | A client disconnect during a three-choice stream aborts all three requests and sends no `[DONE]` |
| `test_sampling_params_are_parsed_from_the_request[completions-non-dict-stream-options-ignored]` | 1 | A non-streaming completion with a list-valued `stream_options` is accepted with default sampling, as the chat case already was |

## How are results checked?

Streaming variants first require the scenario's runtime checks, the same ones the non-streaming test uses, which show that the scenario's feature actually ran. They then check every partial reply:

- the request is still live when its partial is sent;
- each partial carries new tokens, with log probabilities and top-N entries exactly when the request asked for them;
- the streamed tokens are a prefix of the final tokens;
- partials coincide with the steps where the scenario's feature actually ran, for example a CUDA-graph replay, an MTP step or a prefix-cache hit.

The final tokens and scores must match the legacy run within each scenario's tolerance. Suspend/resume cases also require that a request was streamed across the suspend and that the weight refit happened.

The real-engine tests compare streamed output against a greedy or non-streaming baseline of the same request and check that each request ends exactly once. The coordinator test also requires that the first partial arrives while its stream is still open, that prefix caching and chunked prefill both ran on the ranks that served the requests, and that the cancelled request is aborted while its sibling finishes with the baseline tokens. The epoch test requires a partial for every request in every epoch, and boundaries stamped by the real control message.

## Scope

This PR is test-only and is based directly on `main`. It changes `test_dynamic_engine.py`, `test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py` and `test_endpoints_common.py`, and makes no production, functional-test or configuration change. The whole serving/streaming series adds 2,230 net unit-test lines, within the user-approved 2,232.

Details:

- **Harness changes:** the existing async pairwise tests keep their non-streaming path and their MoE and tensor-parallel checks. The only exceptions are the new NVFP4 and expert-TP scenarios, whose experts do not use the NCCL token dispatcher.
- **Shared tokenizer:** it does not define `eod`, so tests that leave `termination_id` unset still run to their token limit, as on `main`.
- **KV handoff test:** it needs exactly two ranks, one prefill and one decode, so it skips at other world sizes. It therefore does not run in the standard 8-GPU or 4-GPU CI jobs; it ran here in dedicated two-rank jobs.
- **Coordinator test on several ranks:** CI launches unit tests on 8 ranks, which gives the coordinator test eight data-parallel engines. The test turns off the load term of the coordinator's routing score, so requests that share a prefix reach the same engine, and it gathers its engine-side checks from every rank after the engines stop. It runs its baseline requests by stepping the engine on its own event loop. Called from inside a running loop, the synchronous `generate()` runs each step on a helper thread that starts on CUDA device 0, which crashed every rank other than 0 with an illegal memory access. That production issue is outside this PR.
- **Narrowed RECOMPUTE refit check:** in `test_async_streaming_survives_suspend_refit_resume[recompute-suspend-resume]` the async run must match the legacy run's tokens exactly and report only finite scores, but no prompt or generated log-prob or top-n values are compared. Since NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#8426, `main` keeps the scores a recomputed request already has, which the legacy run computed before the suspend. The async run drops its pending forward at a RECOMPUTE suspend and rescores after the weight refit, which shifts its prompt scores by up to 0.21 and its generated scores by up to 0.005. Refit's lmcafee-nvidia/Megatron-LM#167 finishes that forward at suspend instead and should restore full parity; tighten this check then. Every other case stays exact.
- **Out of scope:** the production fixes found with this foundation, and the end-to-end SSE and HTTP checks that need several of them, are separate PRs: production fixes #8492, #8594, #8595, #8596, #8597, #8598, #8599, #8600, #8601, lmcafee-nvidia/Megatron-LM#125, and tests lmcafee-nvidia/Megatron-LM#126.

I found three test correctness/coverage issues below and one inline style violation. I reviewed all three changed files and their directly affected contracts. This was static review; I didn't execute tests.

### [P1] Preserve late lookup of the engine class

The new default argument in [_build_test_env](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py#L1676-L1680) captures `DynamicInferenceEngine` at import time. The existing [real_engine fixture](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/disagg_test_utils.py#L69-L106) patches that module symbol to `StateHandoffDynamicInferenceEngine`, then calls the builder without an explicit override. It now receives the base engine instead of the handoff subclass.

For example, [test_disagg_real_engine_parity[nccl-boundary]](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_disagg_pairwise.py#L46-L119) first uses that fixture for its collocated reference; teardown accesses the missing `_kv_transfer_agent` attribute. Role-bearing calls also reach the base engine's [raising setup_kv_transfer stub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/megatron/core/inference/engines/dynamic_engine.py#L717-L719). These unchanged callers worked with the base tree's late-bound construction.

**Correction:** retain both late lookup and explicit class selection. At the builder's signature and start, use:

```python
def _build_test_env(cls, test_config, engine_cls=None):
    if engine_cls is None:
        engine_cls = DynamicInferenceEngine
    clear_nvte_env_vars()
    # Existing body follows unchanged.
```

Keep the existing decorators and the later `engine_cls(...)` construction. This preserves ordinary base-engine construction, patched callers, and the new handoff test's explicit override.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** assert that the existing module-symbol patch produces a `StateHandoffDynamicInferenceEngine` with initialized handoff state; an unpatched call produces the base engine; an explicit subclass override still wins. Run the existing `nccl-boundary` case through successful fixture teardown and retain its transferred-state and final-token parity assertions. The suggested code hasn't been executed; verify it before adopting.

### [P2] Skip only the unavailable NIXL parameter

The new [two-rank KV-handoff test](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py#L4195-L4239) always runs both transport parameters when its rank and FlashAttention guards pass. Without the optional NIXL package, the NIXL row reaches [NixlTransferBackend.__init__](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/megatron/core/inference/disaggregation/transfer_backends/nixl.py#L247-L253) and raises instead of skipping. Existing real-handoff tests already use an [availability guard](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/disagg_test_utils.py#L16-L32).

**Correction:** add this at the start of the test, before either environment is built:

```python
if kv_transport_backend == "nixl":
    from megatron.core.inference.disaggregation.transfer_backends.nixl import _HAVE_NIXL

    if not _HAVE_NIXL:
        pytest.skip("NIXL is not installed")
```

Don't import the shared disaggregation test utility here: it imports this test module. Keep NCCL runnable without NIXL, and retain the existing world-size guard.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** on two ranks without NIXL, only the NIXL row skips; NCCL still checks the KV digest, imported partial and final-token parity. With a compatible NIXL runtime, both rows execute those checks. Non-two-rank launches should retain their existing skips. This source-derived suggestion hasn't been executed; verify it before adopting.

### [P2] Emit a partial before testing suspend/resume continuity

The streaming harness [suspends immediately after its first step](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py#L1791-L1800). In async mode, that first call only launches a primer: the controller explicitly [skips sampling and returns primer_only](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/megatron/core/inference/text_generation_controllers/text_generation_controller.py#L3118-L3124). No partial has been emitted when suspension occurs.

The [final witness](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py#L1826-L1845) therefore proves only that requests stream after resume. It doesn't test continuity of an existing stream. For example, clearing `_partial_emit_lengths` during suspend would duplicate earlier streamed tokens in production, but these cases have no earlier emitted offsets to lose.

**Correction:** in the streaming async variant, advance until a nonempty partial exists before suspending, snapshot those request IDs, then require another partial for at least one of the same IDs after resume. Continue checking the combined history against final tokens. Preserve the non-streaming tests' original sequencing, the pending-forward lifecycle assertions, strict comparisons elsewhere, and the narrowly scoped RECOMPUTE score exception. The exact stepping change needs verification against refit parity because it changes which forward is pending; I wouldn't provide a drop-in patch without that check.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** for the PERSIST `dense-eager-events`, OFFLOAD and RECOMPUTE streaming cases, require nonempty history before `suspend()` and a subsequent partial for the same request after `resume()`. Retain final-token parity and accumulated-prefix equality. As a proposed mutation check, clearing `_partial_emit_lengths` during suspend should make accumulated-prefix equality fail on duplicated tokens. These checks haven't been executed.

> **Note:** formal approval is not available for this request, so this review is posted as a comment only.

detail.body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR adds a unit-test foundation for serving and streaming in dynamic inference. It streams real engine output through the coordinator reply path and the live client APIs, checking each partial reply against the final result and against the same request run without streaming. It changes no production code, and every test passes on unmodified `main`.

The foundation adds:

- streaming variants of the async-scheduling pairwise tests: every single-GPU scenario, the suspend/resume scenarios with a weight refit while suspended, and the distributed scenarios. They run beside the existing non-streaming tests, which are unchanged;
- five new async-pair scenarios: hybrid GDP, hybrid GDN, MXFP8 Transformer Engine, NVFP4 inference-optimized MoE, and MoE with EP2 and expert-TP2;
- real-engine streaming tests:
  - prompt KV handed off between two ranks over NCCL and NIXL;
  - image and video requests on a small LLaVA model;
  - two live clients streaming through a real coordinator, the high-level API facades, and a cancelled request beside a survivor;
  - generation-epoch control messages arriving during streaming;
- endpoint streaming tests: a client disconnect aborts every open stream, and a non-streaming completion ignores a malformed `stream_options` field;
- test infrastructure:
  - a LLaVA model option in the engine test environment, and an engine-class override;
  - configuration fields for expert TP, the MoE expert count, the FP8 recipe, the KV transport backend, the grouped-GEMM backend and the NVFP4 recipe;
  - a shared test tokenizer whose `detokenize` accepts keyword arguments and that resolves an `<image>` token.

## How was the test matrix determined?

An audit of serving coverage found that streaming was tested mainly with simple single-feature requests. Streaming was not crossed with the engine features that change how requests are scheduled, such as prefix caching, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, MTP, hybrid models, MoE, parallel topologies and suspend/resume. The end-to-end paths that only exist with streaming also had no real-engine coverage: disaggregated KV handoff, multimodal media and live coordinator clients.

The matrix has two layers:

1. **Streaming crossed with the async-pair scenarios.** The async-scheduling suite already has one scenario per behavior-affecting feature. The new streaming variant runs each scenario with streaming on and compares the result with the legacy non-streaming run. The five added scenarios extend the suite to model, precision and topology features it did not cover.
2. **Real-engine streaming paths.** These exercise the coordinator, the client, KV handoff and multimodal media with real model steps.
3. **Endpoint streaming.** Two endpoint behaviors that already work on `main` and had no test: a client disconnect during a stream, and a malformed `stream_options` on a non-streaming completion.

This is differential coverage: each streaming run is compared with the non-streaming legacy run of the same scenario. The existing non-streaming async tests still run unchanged, so the async-scheduling coverage on `main` is not replaced.

## What combinations are tested?

### Streaming × single-GPU async scenarios (31 cases)

Each case runs the scenario's requests in the legacy scheduler without streaming, and in the async scheduler with streaming at interval 1. The async engine sends partial replies through a mocked coordinator socket.

| Group | Scenarios |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduling and caching | `dense-eager-events`, `chunked-capacity`, `prefix-ref-zero`, `prefix-lru-chunked` |
| CUDA graphs | `graph-decode-block-exponential`, `graph-bounded-mixed-prefill`, `graph-mixed-layer-linear` |
| Sampling and scores | `sampling-temperature-top-k`, `sampling-top-p`, `sampling-top-k-top-p`, `raw-prompt-top-n-logprobs`, `processed-skip-prompt-logprobs`, `flashinfer-sampling` |
| Lengths and termination | `length-zero-and-total`, `string-prompt-bos`, `termination-values`, `stop-sequence-keep`, `stop-sequence-strip` |
| Speculative decoding | `mtp-depth-one`, `mtp-graph-heterogeneous-logprobs` |
| Models | `hybrid-mamba`, `hybrid-gdp` (new), `hybrid-gdn` (new), `transformer-engine`, `inference-optimized` |
| Precision | `fp8-transformer-engine`, `mxfp8-transformer-engine` (new, Blackwell), `nvfp4-inference-moe` (new, Blackwell) |
| Attention | `flashinfer-fused-rope`, `swa-off-by-one-sink`, `alternating-swa-learnable-sink` |

### Streaming × suspend/resume (2 cases)

While suspended, both the legacy run and the streaming async run load the same perturbed weights from a second model, so their outputs remain comparable after the refit.

| Scenario | Lifecycle while streaming |
| --- | --- |
| `offload-suspend-resume` | Suspend with KV offload, refit the weights from a second model, resume |
| `recompute-suspend-resume` | Suspend with recompute, refit the weights, resume |

### Streaming × distributed topologies (4 cases)

| Scenario | Topology | Ranks |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `tp2-pp2-sp-dp2` | TP2 × PP2 with sequence parallelism, DP2 | 8 |
| `moe-ep2-nccl` | MoE with EP2 and the NCCL token dispatcher | 4 or more |
| `moe-ep2-etp2` (new) | MoE with EP2 and expert TP2, Transformer Engine | 4 or more |
| `optimized-tp2-sp` | Inference-optimized layers with TP2 and sequence parallelism | 4 or more |

### Real-engine streaming paths (6 cases)

| Test | Cases | What it combines |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `test_real_kv_handoff_streams_imported_decode_and_matches_greedy` | 2 (NCCL, NIXL) | One rank prefills, the other imports the KV and streams decode |
| `test_real_vlm_media_stream_matches_nonstreaming` | 2 (image, video) | LLaVA media embeddings with streaming against non-streaming |
| `test_real_coordinator_streams_before_completion_and_matches_greedy` | 1 | Two clients streaming through a real coordinator with chunked prefill and prefix caching; the sync and async high-level facades; cancellation with a surviving request |
| `test_streamed_partials_follow_generation_epoch_messages` | 1 | Generation-epoch control messages while requests stream |

### Endpoint streaming (3 cases)

| Test | Cases | What it checks |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `test_streaming_disconnect_aborts_every_open_stream` | 2 (chat, completions) | A client disconnect during a three-choice stream aborts all three requests and sends no `[DONE]` |
| `test_sampling_params_are_parsed_from_the_request[completions-non-dict-stream-options-ignored]` | 1 | A non-streaming completion with a list-valued `stream_options` is accepted with default sampling, as the chat case already was |

## How are results checked?

Streaming variants first require the scenario's runtime checks, the same ones the non-streaming test uses, which show that the scenario's feature actually ran. They then check every partial reply:

- the request is still live when its partial is sent;
- each partial carries new tokens, with log probabilities and top-N entries exactly when the request asked for them;
- the streamed tokens are a prefix of the final tokens;
- partials coincide with the steps where the scenario's feature actually ran, for example a CUDA-graph replay, an MTP step or a prefix-cache hit.

The final tokens and scores must match the legacy run within each scenario's tolerance. Suspend/resume cases also require that a request was streamed across the suspend and that the weight refit happened.

The real-engine tests compare streamed output against a greedy or non-streaming baseline of the same request and check that each request ends exactly once. The coordinator test also requires that the first partial arrives while its stream is still open, that prefix caching and chunked prefill both ran on the ranks that served the requests, and that the cancelled request is aborted while its sibling finishes with the baseline tokens. The epoch test requires a partial for every request in every epoch, and boundaries stamped by the real control message.

## Scope

This PR is test-only and is based directly on `main`. It changes `test_dynamic_engine.py`, `test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py` and `test_endpoints_common.py`, and makes no production, functional-test or configuration change. The whole serving/streaming series adds 2,230 net unit-test lines, within the user-approved 2,232.

Details:

- **Harness changes:** the existing async pairwise tests keep their non-streaming path and their MoE and tensor-parallel checks. The only exceptions are the new NVFP4 and expert-TP scenarios, whose experts do not use the NCCL token dispatcher.
- **Shared tokenizer:** it does not define `eod`, so tests that leave `termination_id` unset still run to their token limit, as on `main`.
- **KV handoff test:** it needs exactly two ranks, one prefill and one decode, so it skips at other world sizes. It therefore does not run in the standard 8-GPU or 4-GPU CI jobs; it ran here in dedicated two-rank jobs.
- **Coordinator test on several ranks:** CI launches unit tests on 8 ranks, which gives the coordinator test eight data-parallel engines. The test turns off the load term of the coordinator's routing score, so requests that share a prefix reach the same engine, and it gathers its engine-side checks from every rank after the engines stop. It runs its baseline requests by stepping the engine on its own event loop. Called from inside a running loop, the synchronous `generate()` runs each step on a helper thread that starts on CUDA device 0, which crashed every rank other than 0 with an illegal memory access. That production issue is outside this PR.
- **Narrowed RECOMPUTE refit check:** in `test_async_streaming_survives_suspend_refit_resume[recompute-suspend-resume]` the async run must match the legacy run's tokens exactly and report only finite scores, but no prompt or generated log-prob or top-n values are compared. Since NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#8426, `main` keeps the scores a recomputed request already has, which the legacy run computed before the suspend. The async run drops its pending forward at a RECOMPUTE suspend and rescores after the weight refit, which shifts its prompt scores by up to 0.21 and its generated scores by up to 0.005. Refit's lmcafee-nvidia/Megatron-LM#167 finishes that forward at suspend instead and should restore full parity; tighten this check then. Every other case stays exact.
- **Out of scope:** the production fixes found with this foundation, and the end-to-end SSE and HTTP checks that need several of them, are separate PRs: production fixes #8492, #8594, #8595, #8596, #8597, #8598, #8599, #8600, #8601, lmcafee-nvidia/Megatron-LM#125, and tests lmcafee-nvidia/Megatron-LM#126.

## Validation

Exact tested commit: `cf2a8f7361022168e27654f86116c24c344ed12e`. It merges NVIDIA `main` at `01fa4164c8b539958500c2314ad52eacfdd80774` into `60032c99`. The only conflict was in the imports of `test_dynamic_engine.py`. The merge keeps both sides, this PR's `deepcopy` and `wraps` and `main`'s `dataclasses.replace`, and changes nothing else.

Results at this commit, in the GitHub CI image (`mcore-ci-dev-main-20261026T1651Z`: FA4, no FA3), H100, 8 ranks, CI's pytest command (PDX job 7853290), compared test by test with `main` at `01fa4164` in the same image (PDX job 7853291). Counts are unique tests across the 8 ranks, as passed/failed/skipped.

| Module | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_dynamic_engine.py` | 308/0/2 | 312/0/4 |
| `test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py` | 87/0/0 | 125/0/4 |
| `test_endpoints_common.py` | 68/0/0 | 71/0/0 |

- No test that passes on `main` fails here, and no `main` test is missing. The 2 extra `test_dynamic_engine.py` skips are the KV handoff cases, which need two ranks. The async skips are the MXFP8 and NVFP4 rows, which need Blackwell.
- Both RECOMPUTE and OFFLOAD refit streaming cases, `test_real_coordinator_streams_before_completion_and_matches_greedy`, both `test_real_vlm_media_stream_matches_nonstreaming` cases and `test_streamed_partials_follow_generation_epoch_messages` passed on every rank.
- Black 26.3.0, isort 5.13.2, Ruff, `py_compile` and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files.

Before that, `5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7` merged NVIDIA `main` at `90f4d5279b951a408d7bf605a24776c248357c03` into `2ca9494b` (through an earlier merge of `58124853`). Those merges resolved conflicts only in `test_dynamic_engine.py` and kept both sides: this PR's `fp8_recipe` field and MLP-projection imports, and `main`'s batch-invariant attention settings. Two follow-up test-only commits came out of the CI-image run below:

- `test_real_vlm_media_stream_matches_nonstreaming` accepts `main`'s deferred image encoding. Since NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#8408, `main` encodes waiting images together before prefill, so an image request has no embeddings right after submission, and the test had failed on every rank. The in-step injection check still compares the injected embeddings.
- The RECOMPUTE refit streaming case compares tokens and finite scores only, as described under Scope.

### [P1] Preserve late lookup of the engine class

The new default argument in [_build_test_env](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py#L1676-L1680) captures `DynamicInferenceEngine` at import time. The existing [real_engine fixture](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/disagg_test_utils.py#L69-L106) patches that module symbol to `StateHandoffDynamicInferenceEngine`, then calls the builder without an explicit override. It now receives the base engine instead of the handoff subclass.

For example, [test_disagg_real_engine_parity[nccl-boundary]](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_disagg_pairwise.py#L46-L119) first uses that fixture for its collocated reference; teardown accesses the missing `_kv_transfer_agent` attribute. Role-bearing calls also reach the base engine's [raising setup_kv_transfer stub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/megatron/core/inference/engines/dynamic_engine.py#L717-L719). These unchanged callers worked with the base tree's late-bound construction.

**Correction:** retain both late lookup and explicit class selection. At the builder's signature and start, use:

```python
def _build_test_env(cls, test_config, engine_cls=None):
    if engine_cls is None:
        engine_cls = DynamicInferenceEngine
    clear_nvte_env_vars()
    # Existing body follows unchanged.
```

Keep the existing decorators and the later `engine_cls(...)` construction. This preserves ordinary base-engine construction, patched callers, and the new handoff test's explicit override.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** assert that the existing module-symbol patch produces a `StateHandoffDynamicInferenceEngine` with initialized handoff state; an unpatched call produces the base engine; an explicit subclass override still wins. Run the existing `nccl-boundary` case through successful fixture teardown and retain its transferred-state and final-token parity assertions. The suggested code hasn't been executed; verify it before adopting.

### [P2] Skip only the unavailable NIXL parameter

The new [two-rank KV-handoff test](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py#L4195-L4239) always runs both transport parameters when its rank and FlashAttention guards pass. Without the optional NIXL package, the NIXL row reaches [NixlTransferBackend.__init__](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/megatron/core/inference/disaggregation/transfer_backends/nixl.py#L247-L253) and raises instead of skipping. Existing real-handoff tests already use an [availability guard](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/disagg_test_utils.py#L16-L32).

```python
if kv_transport_backend == "nixl":
    from megatron.core.inference.disaggregation.transfer_backends.nixl import _HAVE_NIXL

    if not _HAVE_NIXL:
        pytest.skip("NIXL is not installed")
```

Don't import the shared disaggregation test utility here: it imports this test module. Keep NCCL runnable without NIXL, and retain the existing world-size guard.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** on two ranks without NIXL, only the NIXL row skips; NCCL still checks the KV digest, imported partial and final-token parity. With a compatible NIXL runtime, both rows execute those checks. Non-two-rank launches should retain their existing skips. This source-derived suggestion hasn't been executed; verify it before adopting.

### [P2] Emit a partial before testing suspend/resume continuity

The streaming harness [suspends immediately after its first step](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine_async_sched.py#L1791-L1800). In async mode, that first call only launches a primer: the controller explicitly [skips sampling and returns primer_only](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5b99e5450cc95cc6561feb6aae2cab0cfde015c7/megatron/core/inference/text_generation_controllers/text_generation_controller.py#L3118-L3124). No partial has been emitted when suspension occurs.

It doesn't test continuity of an existing stream. For example, clearing `_partial_emit_lengths` during suspend would duplicate earlier streamed tokens in production, but these cases have no earlier emitted offsets to lose.

**Correction:** in the streaming async variant, advance until a nonempty partial exists before suspending, snapshot those request IDs, then require another partial for at least one of the same IDs after resume. Continue checking the combined history against final tokens. Preserve the non-streaming tests' original sequencing, the pending-forward lifecycle assertions, strict comparisons elsewhere, and the narrowly scoped RECOMPUTE score exception. The exact stepping change needs verification against refit parity because it changes which forward is pending; I wouldn't provide a drop-in patch without that check.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** for the PERSIST `dense-eager-events`, OFFLOAD and RECOMPUTE streaming cases, require nonempty history before `suspend()` and a subsequent partial for the same request after `resume()`. Retain final-token parity and accumulated-prefix equality. As a proposed mutation check, clearing `_partial_emit_lengths` during suspend should make accumulated-prefix equality fail on duplicated tokens. These checks haven't been executed.
